statement: The four opt-in ticket properties are read by two implementations: the Rust core, which decides what a project accepts and what the CLI and the app may write, and the frontend, which decides what a stored value renders as and what a control offers. Both are written from this table, so a rule changed on one side and not the other fails here rather than in a project's files.

fibonacciScale.note: Fixed, and the one estimate system with nothing to configure: a project on Fibonacci has no `values` of its own. The order is the order a control offers.

durations.note: One number and one unit. Compounds are refused because two units in one value make its meaning depend on `hours_per_day`, which the project can change under the ticket; decimals carry that case instead. A zero amount is not a duration — it is the shape of a value nobody meant to write, and it is the case the two implementations had drifted on.

cases.note: decimals carry what compounds may not
no ceiling: the format states none
a zero amount is not a duration
a compound, whose meaning would move with the project's conversion
a unit the grammar does not have
a leading point is a number this format does not write
Arabic-Indic digits are digits to neither side

conversions.note: How a duration orders against another duration. The two rates are project settings, so this table states the defaults and the arithmetic, not a fixed minute count per unit.

defaults.note: What a project file that omits these keys reads as. The frontend carries the same three in `NO_PROPERTIES`, which is what a project with no `properties:` block looks like to a surface.

tshirtScale.note: Seeded rather than fixed: this is what `properties.estimate.values` holds when Estimate is first enabled, and a project that deletes a rung keeps it deleted. Both sides state the seed so a control's fallback and the writer's seed cannot disagree.

estimateSystems.note: A project is on exactly one. `tshirt` is the default because its vocabulary is the one already in the file, so a bare `enabled: true` is usable rather than a project that refuses to open over a missing key.

dates.note: What the format stores for `due` and `start`: exactly `YYYY-MM-DD`, and a day the calendar has. Strict about width because `2026-9-8` and `2026-09-08` would otherwise both be written and only one of them sorts as text.

cases.note: a leap day in a leap year
the width is part of the grammar
